name: Basalt Crust
description: The product standing on the cooling crust of a pahoehoe lava flow at dusk, incandescent orange fissures breaking open close beside it and lighting it from below while cool blue ambient falls from above. Heat shimmer distorts the air over the hottest cracks — the danger is a hand-span away, not on the horizon.
lighting: Incandescent fissure underlight, cool dusk ambient
subject: product
prompt: a heavy smoked-black glass flask with a dark gunmetal cap, the product is the hero of the frame and occupies roughly 55 percent of the frame height, tack-sharp and clearly lit, standing on the cooling crust of a pahoehoe lava flow at dusk, the crust a skin of black basalt folded into real coiled rope-and-entrail texture with a fine silver-grey glassy bloom across its upper surfaces, hairline cooling cracks and small collapsed plates tilted where the flow has drained beneath them, incandescent orange-to-white fissures breaking open across the crust close beside the product and lighting the scene from below so the underside of the flask and the near rope folds carry the warm key while everything above falls into cold blue dusk ambient, genuine heat shimmer rising over the hottest cracks and distorting only what is seen through it, thin dark smoke drifting low and sparse, colour running from incandescent yellow-white in the fissure cores through deep orange and ember red to near-black basalt and cold blue shadow with nothing in between, the flow treated as supporting texture cropped tight at crust scale rather than shown as a wide volcanic landscape, no open flame, no fountaining or spattering lava, no distant smoking cone or horizon, no ash fall, no molten liquid touching the product, the crust genuinely solid under the product with a true contact shadow bridged by the glow, believable radiant-heat falloff, no second product, cinematic elemental realism
